method: Retrieved the page, identified revision 273249 and retained an unchanged fixed-revision HTML retrieval. Decoded all p/h3 blocks exactly. Observed every bracketed decimal marker, preserving Arabic digit glyphs and duplicate occurrences. Partitioned every decoded source code point into reversible spans. This is lexical coverage, not approved report boundaries or proof of narration completeness.

findings.finding: Two newline characters precede each number. The old beginning-of-paragraph matcher would attach these paragraphs to the preceding report.

Raw wikitext for an odd-number-of-stones chapter is followed immediately by an Arabic-digit 162 marker. A later paragraph has another 162 label. No 160 marker is observed. The heading, original glyphs, duplicate and sequence are all preserved; no automatic renumbering was performed.
Each HTML paragraph contains two numbered markers. One paragraph cannot be assumed to be one report.

Unnumbered chapter context and marker 239 share a paragraph. The old importer treated the whole paragraph as chapter context. No claim that this chapter is numberless can be made from that old classification.

comparisonOrientation.observed: The English comparison separately lists the later numbers that the old paragraph-start matcher missed. Its final Ablution reference is 244; the next selected Arabic book begins at 245. These observations orient the next edition map; they do not approve the Arabic body, assign 160 to the repeated 162 marker, or establish equivalence with other numbering systems.

safeguard: Both ordinary Wikisource importers now refuse embedded, malformed, nonstandard or repeated numeric markers and unrendered heading syntax before inferring report ownership. A separate pending layout registry retains irregular candidates without making them reader-eligible. Existing Faith and Knowledge inventories remain byte-for-byte reproducible.
